newsitem.title: USA: Strike settled at IBP Illinois beef plant.
newsitem.headline: Strike settled at IBP Illinois beef plant.

text.p: Union employees at IBP Inc's Joslin, Ill., beef plant accepted a new labor contract Friday, which will allow the beef plant to gradually restart operations beginning Saturday, the company said in a release.
The agreement ended a strike, which closed the plant for two weeks. Some crews, including plant maintenance, return to work Saturday, while beef processing crews gradually return Monday and Tuesday.

The contract takes effect immediately for the plant's 1,800 employees who are members of the United Food and Commercial Workers union local 1540. It provides an $0.80 per hour pay increase in the base wage over the next 36 months, including an immediate $0.40 increase.
The deal also provides a profit-sharing program after an annual deduction of $480 per employee. Terms of a prescription drug program will be determined later by a federal mediator.
